Here's an argument you can bring up for people against deregulation of suppressors.

One common thing brought up is some variation of "just use hearing protection"

Well, looking at

Www.Coopersafety.com/noisereduction.aspx

We find that the NRR rating of plugs and earmuffs is not simply subtracted from the dB of the noise.

You first minus 7 and divide by 2. So with plugs with an NRR rating of 33, you minus 13 dB from the source dB. If the gun you are shooting makes a 150 dB sound, the sound reaching your ears is 137 dB...still much too loud and capable of damaging your hearing with prolonged use.

And as for doubling up, plugs AND muffs? Well again not so simple. The NRR ratings don't add. You just add 5 to the one with the higher rating. So putting 22 NRR muffs OVER 33 NRR plugs, it becomes only 38 NRR worth of protection. So that 150 dB shot is at 134.5 dB, STILL plenty high enough to cause damage.

The thing is, not many people double up as they should and 150 dB isn't THAT loud as far as of gun shots go. There's guns in the 160 dB range and remember, the dB scale is logarithmic. Because it's a logarithmic scale we perceive the sound being dampened by a large amount... But there's still plenty of damage being done even when you're doing everything by the book.

So, assuming you have a suppressed 9mm at about 125 dB, doubling up on ear pro with the setup above you're still getting 109.5 dB...crazy huh? Louder than a chain saw.

To your brain the sound might be miniscule. The brain perceives sound waves differently. But your ears can't tell the difference, it's all energy doing damage all the same.
